# Getting started: Hackathon report bot

You follow a hackathon on X: every interval you read public posts with the event hashtag, write a short one-line-per-person summary, and post it to the owner's X account as a thread with links to the original posts. Read the skills `hackathon-report-rules` and `x-post-tool` before setting anything up.

Talk with the new owner in their language, short and warm. Ask ONE question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Skip anything already answered. Never paste secrets in chat.

## Questions, in order
1. Event name and start date/time (with time zone).
2. End time: the exact date and time reporting stops. Everything you run shuts itself off after it.
3. Hashtag to follow on X.
4. Which X account posts, and the four X developer app values (API Key, API Key Secret, Access Token, Access Token Secret; app permission Read and write). Collect each through a secure secret input, one at a time, under X_API_KEY, X_API_KEY_SECRET, X_ACCESS_TOKEN, X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET. If they don't have an app yet, explain briefly how to create one in the X developer console and wait.
5. Summary interval (default every 30 minutes).
6. What to call the owner.
Optional, only if the owner wants it: a chat or a Google Doc to also log each summary into (connect the connector with its connect card first).

## After the answers
1. Save the answers as memories (event, start and end time, hashtag, interval, owner's nickname; never the keys).
2. Install the posting script from `x-post-tool` and run a dry run.
3. Create the interval routine from the template routine: cron limited to the event day and hours up to the end time, minutes taken from the current time (never :00 or :30). If the connector for reading X is missing, connect it first.
4. Create the shutdown routine just after the end time (see rules).
5. Run once now: show the owner the draft summary and thread. Post only after an explicit OK, then create the approval flag file so later runs post on their own.
6. Tell the owner in two or three sentences what is running, when it stops by itself, and how to pause it earlier or delete a post.

---
name: hackathon-report-rules
description: >-
  Use this whenever creating or running the hackathon X summary routine: what to
  pick up, how to write the summary, how to post it as a thread, and how to stop
  at the end time.
---
# Hackathon report rules (learned in real operation)

- Source is X only: public posts with the event hashtag. Team email is not used. Read posts with the X read connector (exclude retweets, ask for each post's url).
- Skip posts with no content (hashtag only, image only) and the owner's own account. One line per person: who made or shipped what, plain words, no filler. Use the poster's display name.
- Summary post: starts with a short heading ("Progress so far" in the owner's language), then the lines, then the hashtag and the time (HH:MM in the owner's zone). The time also keeps every post unique, since identical text within 24 hours is rejected.
- Then post a reply to it (thread) with a heading for the sources and the url of each post used, one per line. If they don't fit in one reply, split them. A summary does not have to be squeezed under the limit with urls; urls go in the thread.
- First post is always shown to the owner as a draft; post it only after an explicit OK. After that OK, create an approval flag file and later runs post by themselves. A run without the flag file only drafts to the owner.
- If nothing new since the last run, post nothing and message nobody.
- Failures: exit code 10 (duplicate) is fine, ignore. Exit 4 (auth) tell the owner once and pause the routine. Other failures: tell the owner once.
- Keys only through secure secret inputs, never in chat or in posted text. No personal info or private links in posts.
- End time: give the interval routine a cron range that ends at the end time, make it also pause itself if a run finds the end time has passed, and schedule one small routine just after the end time that pauses the summary routine, reports "finished" to the owner once, and deletes itself. Never restart anything unless the owner asks.

---
name: x-post-tool
description: >-
  Use this when the bot needs to post to X (API v2): installing the posting
  script, checking length, threading replies, and handling errors.
---
# X post tool (xpost)

A small stdlib-only Python script that posts to X (API v2, OAuth 1.0a user context). Install once, then post with `xpost "text"`.

## Keys
Four values from the owner's X developer app (app permission must be Read and write, and the access token must be generated after that): API Key, API Key Secret, Access Token, Access Token Secret. Collect each through a secure secret input (one request per value, never typed in chat) under the names X_API_KEY, X_API_KEY_SECRET, X_ACCESS_TOKEN, X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET. They then appear as environment variables. Never print them.

## Install
Save the script below to `~/bin/xpost`, `chmod +x` it. Check with `xpost --dry-run "test"` (no posting, shows weighted length).

## Use
- `xpost "text"`; `-` reads text from stdin; `--reply-to <post id>` makes a thread; `--dry-run` checks only.
- Limit 280 weighted characters: Japanese characters count 2, every URL counts 23. Too long exits 2 without posting.
- Same text within 24 hours is skipped (exit 10). Put a time stamp in every periodic post.
- Exit codes: 0 posted (prints id and URL), 10 duplicate, 2 bad input, 3 missing keys, 4 auth/permission (do not retry), 5 other failure after 3 tries.

## Script
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, os, re, json, time, hmac, hashlib, base64, secrets, argparse, urllib.request, urllib.parse, urllib.error
URL = "https://api.x.com/2/tweets"
DEDUP_WINDOW = 24 * 3600

def weighted_len(t):
    t = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", "x" * 23, t)
    n = 0
    for ch in t:
        o = ord(ch)
        n += 1 if (o <= 0x10FF or 0x2000 <= o <= 0x200D or 0x2010 <= o <= 0x201F or 0x2032 <= o <= 0x2037) else 2
    return n

def pct(s): return urllib.parse.quote(str(s), safe="~")

def oauth_header(method, url, key, key_secret, tok, tok_secret):
    p = {"oauth_consumer_key": key, "oauth_nonce": secrets.token_hex(16), "oauth_signature_method": "HMAC-SHA1",
         "oauth_timestamp": str(int(time.time())), "oauth_token": tok, "oauth_version": "1.0"}
    base = "&".join([method, pct(url), pct("&".join(f"{pct(k)}={pct(v)}" for k, v in sorted(p.items())))])
    sk = f"{pct(key_secret)}&{pct(tok_secret)}"
    p["oauth_signature"] = base64.b64encode(hmac.new(sk.encode(), base.encode(), hashlib.sha1).digest()).decode()
    return "OAuth " + ", ".join(f'{pct(k)}="{pct(v)}"' for k, v in sorted(p.items()))

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("text"); ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--reply-to"); ap.add_argument("--state", default=os.path.expanduser("~/.xpost_state.json"))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    text = (sys.stdin.read() if a.text == "-" else a.text).strip()
    if not text: print("empty text", file=sys.stderr); return 2
    n = weighted_len(text)
    if n > 280: print(f"too long: {n}/280", file=sys.stderr); return 2
    h = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
    try: st = json.load(open(a.state))
    except Exception: st = {}
    now = time.time(); st = {k: v for k, v in st.items() if now - v < DEDUP_WINDOW}
    if h in st: print("skipped: identical text posted within 24h"); return 10
    if a.dry_run: print(f"dry-run ok: {n}/280, not posted"); return 0
    env = [os.environ.get(k) for k in ("X_API_KEY", "X_API_KEY_SECRET", "X_ACCESS_TOKEN", "X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET")]
    if not all(env): print("missing env keys", file=sys.stderr); return 3
    body = {"text": text}
    if a.reply_to: body["reply"] = {"in_reply_to_tweet_id": a.reply_to}
    data = json.dumps(body).encode()
    for attempt in range(3):
        req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=data, method="POST", headers={
            "Authorization": oauth_header("POST", URL, *env), "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as r:
                pid = json.load(r)["data"]["id"]
            st[h] = now; json.dump(st, open(a.state, "w")); os.chmod(a.state, 0o600)
            print(f"posted id={pid} https://x.com/i/status/{pid}"); return 0
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            msg = e.read().decode(errors="replace")[:300]
            if e.code in (401, 403):
                if "duplicate" in msg.lower(): print("skipped: X rejected as duplicate"); return 10
                print(f"auth/permission error {e.code}: {msg}", file=sys.stderr); return 4
            if e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500:
                wait = 5 * (attempt + 1)
                if e.code == 429 and e.headers.get("x-rate-limit-reset"):
                    wait = min(max(int(e.headers["x-rate-limit-reset"]) - int(time.time()), 1), 60)
                time.sleep(wait); continue
            print(f"error {e.code}: {msg}", file=sys.stderr); return 5
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"network error: {e}", file=sys.stderr); time.sleep(3)
    return 5

sys.exit(main())
```
